g.text: It is not a queue - it is a log with a cursor per reader
Consuming a message mutates nothing; it moves an integer. That one substitution is what makes sequential-only I/O possible.
What a traditional queue must track
Per-message MUTABLE state: small, and randomly
accessed. So every acknowledgement is a RANDOM
WRITE - which locks you into 0.61 MB/sec.
Ten groups reading the same partition read the SAME BYTES. Nothing is copied per subscriber -
each group costs one integer. Replay is 'set your offset backwards'; retention is free because
Not a tuning difference - a different regime.
500 MB/sec needs ~800 drives with random I/O,
"Disk is slow" is one of the most misleading pieces of received wisdom in systems design. Disk is slow FOR RANDOM ACCESS.
So the whole storage engine is organised around one rule: never do a random write, and avoid random reads.
not a copy of the data.
500 MB/sec sustained = 43.2 TB/day = 605 TB at 14-day retention = 1.81 PB at replication factor 3.
Answering 'design a message queue' with a queue is answering a smaller question than the one asked.
